title: Completion equivalence on a closed thickening reflects zero coherent submodules
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], $I,K$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaves, and $q\geq1$. Put $Z=V(K^q)$. Assume completion with respect to $I\mathcal O_Z$ is an equivalence for every Noetherian instance on $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Let $F,H$ be coherent modules and $j:H\hookrightarrow F$ a monomorphism. If $K^qF=0$ and $H/I^{n+1}H=0$ for every $n\geq0$, then $H=0$. Products and quotients use the shared image and cokernel definitions [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module].

proof.text: On every affine open, the power-product zero criterion identifies K^qF=0 with annihilation of F(U) by K(U)^q. The inclusion j is injective on sections, so the same ideal annihilates H(U). The criterion at exponent one, the ideal-power section formula and ker(subscheme inclusion)=K^q identify H as supported on Z.

The coherent closed-pushforward equivalence provides L on Z and an isomorphism H ≅ i_*L. Its natural completion comparison identifies the completed quotient diagram of H with the pushed completed diagram of L.

All components of the completed H diagram are zero. Evaluate the comparison at each level; fully faithful closed pushforward reflects zero. The full inclusion of coherent formal systems reflects zero, hence completion(L) is zero.

Install the Noetherian instance on Z supplied by its closed immersion and use the assumed completion equivalence to reflect zero of L. The coherent inclusion and closed pushforward preserve zero, so the comparison isomorphism gives H=0.
